notes: §1985:VI.6.22.3 SR4 requires, in format 2, that each data-name-1 and data-name-2 'must be subscripted by the first index-name associated with identifier-1 along with other subscripts as required', that a condition-name be defined with a single value, and that its data-name be in the KEY IS phrase. SearchAllFormat2Rules enforces every one of those at 85, each probed: a condition-name with two values or a THRU range, a condition-name on a non-key item, a key operand not in the KEY IS phrase or subscripted by a second index-name (COBOL1965, cited ISO §1985:VI.6.22.3 SR4), a literal or a data-name, a sending identifier that is a key or is subscripted by the first index-name, and a key referenced without its preceding key (COBOL1965, COBOL1966); a qualified key, a key in an inner table with its outer subscript and two keys joined by AND are accepted. The two sentences §2002:14.8.34.2 SR6 and SR7 add (the index-name subscript 'shall not be followed by a' + or -; a condition-name 'shall be subscripted by the first index-name') are not in the 1985 text, so FirstEditionWithSubscriptSentences (2002) leaves them out below 2002: at --std 85 WHEN K (IX + 1) = 2 and WHEN C1 (JX) with C1 on the key compile and run (the accepted golden 1985-SR-VI_6_22_3-4-relative-subscript), and the 2002, 2014 and 2023 refusals stay (pb445-search-all-when-index-plus, pb445-search-all-condition-name-index-plus), each citing its own edition's rule (kb/Work PB5193).

next.reason: 1985: "must be subscripted by the first index-name associated with identifier-1 along with other subscripts as required"; 2023: "The index-name subscript shall not be followed by a '+' or a '-'. ... condition-names ... shall be subscripted by the first index-name". The rules match in substance, but 2023 adds two refusals: relative indexing on the key's index-name subscript, and condition-names not subscripted by the first index-name.
